user.title: New charge controller
user.description:
**How it works**
Every few seconds (10 s by default) the controller reads its **inputs**, decides how fast the car may charge, and sets its **outputs**.

- **Inputs** (only read): what the charger reports, the house power, and optionally the battery level, the electricity price and an EMS signal.
- **Outputs** (written): two entities of your charger's own integration, the charging current limit and the phase setting.

A new controller starts in **shadow mode**: it shows what it would set, but writes nothing until you switch on **Control charger** on its device.

**Steps**
1. Outputs: what the controller changes
2. Outputs: phase options
3. Inputs: the charger
4. Charger limits and safety
5. Inputs: the house
6. Inputs: the car (optional)
7. Inputs: price and EMS (optional)
8. Tuning

data_description.name: The name of the controller device, for example where the charger is. Its entities are named after it.
data_description.import_yaml: The EV Load Balancer YAML package is installed. On: the next steps are prefilled with its entities and values, and the new device starts with its settings. Control charger stays off. You check every step before saving.

outputs.title: 1/8 Outputs: what the controller changes
outputs.description:
**Outputs** are entities the controller changes. It writes to them only while **Control charger** is on.

Pick the two entities of your charger's own integration that set its charging current and its number of phases. Another charge controller cannot use the same entities.

data_description.current_limit_entity: A number entity in A that limits the charging current. Examples: Alfen Max Current Limit S1, go-e Requested current.
data_description.phase_select_entity: The entity that switches the charger between 1 and 3 phases: a select (with options), a switch (on/off) or a number (a value per phase count). The next step asks how it says 1 and 3 phases. Example: Alfen Usable phases (select).

phases.title: 2/8 Outputs: phase options
phases.description: How the phase setting says 1 phase and 3 phases. This depends on your charger's integration: a select has its own option texts, a switch is on or off, and a number has a value per phase count.

data.phase_switch_on: When the switch is on, the charger uses

data_description.phase_option_3: Optional. Leave empty for a charger that only charges on 1 phase: Single phase only is then always on, and the fallback phases must be 1.
data_description.phase_switch_on: For example, a switch named Force single phase is on for 1 phase.
data_description.phase_value_3: Optional. Leave empty for a charger that only charges on 1 phase: Single phase only is then always on, and the fallback phases must be 1.

inputs.title: 3/8 Inputs: the charger
inputs.description:
**Inputs** are entities the controller only reads. It never changes them.

Pick the sensors of your charger's own integration that show its state. The controller uses them to see whether a car is connected and what the charger does now.

data_description.connection_entity: Shows whether a car is connected: a Mode 3 sensor (A, B1–D2, E, F), or a binary sensor that is on while a car is connected. Alfen: Mode 3 State.
data_description.charger_power_entity: The power the charger delivers now, in W or kW. Alfen: Real power sum.
data_description.applied_current_entity: The current limit the charger applies now, in A. Not the current the car draws. Alfen: Actual applied max current.
data_description.active_phases_entity: The number of phases the charger uses now: 1 or 3, or the same texts as the phase setting. Alfen: Charging Mode.
data_description.max_current_entity: The highest current the charger allows, for example its installation maximum. Until it has a value, the fallback current is the maximum. Never above 32 A. Alfen: Actual max current.
data_description.charger_energy_entity: Optional. The charger's energy meter in kWh, for the charged-energy sensors. Empty: the energy is calculated from the charging power.

limits.title: 4/8 Charger limits and safety
limits.description: Fixed values, no entities. They describe your charger and what it gets when something goes wrong. The defaults fit most chargers.

data.failsafe_keeps_phase: Keep the phases on a sensor fault
data.control_off_action: When Control charger is switched off

data_description.min_current_a: The lowest current at which a car charges, usually 6 A. Below it, the controller stops charging.
data_description.voltage_v: The nominal voltage of one phase, usually 230 V.
data_description.current_step_a: The smallest current change the charger accepts.
data_description.widen_small_decreases: Turn on for Alfen chargers: they ignore some decreases of 0.1 A.
data_description.fallback_current_a: The safe current after a sensor fault, and the start current after the car is unplugged.
data_description.fallback_phase: The safe number of phases after a sensor fault, and after the car is unplugged.
data_description.failsafe_keeps_phase: Off (recommended): a sensor fault switches to the fallback phases, so a charger that stops responding is not left on an unintended phase. On: the phases stay as they are.
data_description.control_off_action: What the charger gets once when you switch Control charger off.

household.title: 5/8 Inputs: the house
household.description:
**Inputs** are entities the controller only reads. It never changes them.

The controller gives the car the power that the house leaves under the power limit. Solar export counts as extra power. The power limit comes from an entity, so a helper or your EMS decides it.

data_description.house_power_entity: The grid power of the house without the charger, in W or kW: positive while importing, negative while exporting. Make a template sensor (grid power − charger power) if you only have a grid meter. A sensor smoothed over about 15 s works best.
data_description.solar_power_entity: Optional. Shown in the diagnostics only: the controller finds the solar surplus in the house power.
data_description.power_limit_entity: The most power the house may take from the grid, charger included, in W or kW: a helper or an entity of your EMS. With the capacity tariff, use a limit with a floor, for example max(5000 W, 90 % of this month's peak). A raw monthly peak resets at the start of the month (to 2.5 kW in Flanders) and would limit charging hard. When the entity is unavailable, the last value is used. Until it has a value, the controller writes nothing.
data_description.peak_factor_pct: Optional safety buffer: the controller uses this share of the power limit, for example 90 % to stay below the peak. Leave empty (100 %) when the limit entity already has a buffer.

car.title: 6/8 Inputs: the car (optional)
car.description:
**Inputs** are entities the controller only reads. It never changes them.

With the battery level, the controller stops at a target, charges urgently below an emergency level, and switches Comfort mode to solar. Leave the fields empty without car data.

data_description.car_soc_entity: A sensor with the car's battery level in %, usually from the car's own integration.
data_description.car_max_current_a: The highest current per phase that the car accepts.
data_description.car_min_current_a: The lowest current per phase that the car accepts.

price.title: 7/8 Inputs: price and EMS (optional)
price.description:
**Inputs** are entities the controller only reads. It never changes them.

They allow or limit charging from the grid. Empty: the price check is skipped and no EMS limits the grid.

data_description.price_entity: The import price per kWh. Above Max charging cost, the car does not use the grid.
data_description.price_attribute: Leave empty to use the sensor state. Fill in when the price is an attribute, for example rate_import.
data_description.ems_entity: A power sensor of your EMS. 0 W blocks the grid. How the value is used is set on the device: EMS control turns it on, EMS as on/off chooses between a watt budget (off: the car takes at most this much from the grid) and on/off (on: any value above 0 W allows the grid).

tuning.title: 8/8 Tuning
tuning.description: Fixed values that rarely need a change.

data_description.power_update_threshold_w: An increase is written only when it adds at least this much power, so solar ripple causes no writes. Decreases are always written.
data_description.phase_switch_delay_min: After a change to 1 phase, wait this long before going back to 3 phases.
data_description.recalc_interval_s: How often the controller calculates. Mode, setting, connection and phase changes start a calculation at once.

shared.title: Inputs shared with another controller

error.min_above_max: The min current is higher than the max current.
error.fallback_out_of_range: The fallback current must be between the min and max current.
error.connection_not_mode3: This sensor does not show a Mode 3 state (A, B1–D2, E, F). Pick a Mode 3 sensor or a binary sensor.
error.phase_select_unavailable: The phase setting has no options. Check that the charger is online.
error.current_entity_in_use: Another charge controller already uses this current limit.
error.phase_entity_in_use: Another charge controller already uses this phase setting.
error.capacity_required: Enter the battery capacity when you pick a battery level sensor.
error.car_min_above_max: The car min current is higher than the car max current.
error.attribute_without_price: Pick a price sensor to use a price attribute.
error.price_attribute_missing: The price sensor has no attribute with this name.
error.fallback_needs_three_phases: The charger has no 3-phase option: the fallback phases must be 1 phase.

single_phase_conflicts_mode.message: Single phase only is not possible while the charge mode is 3-Phases Minimum.

charger_not_responding.title: {name}: the charger does not respond
charger_not_responding.description:
The charger did not follow the last 3 writes: its applied current or active phases did not change in time. The controller tries again at each run, and this issue closes when the charger follows again.

Check that the charger is online and that its integration works. To stop the attempts, switch Control charger off.
